P13k1: The Zapatistas also aren't proof of my complete economic path, which goes from unpriced internal necessities, to a common purse, to getting rid of outside money. Their communities do put collective work into supporting their schools and clinics, their autonomous government and their resistance, but they also sell products and trade, and they receive outside support. What they have shown is that major necessities and public functions can be taken out of ordinary market purchase and governed collectively. Outside help can build up a community's capability, but it can also create gatekeepers and uneven dependence when the specialist or donor or organization stays indispensable.
